facts.statement: The generic name Kaijiangosaurus refers to the River Kai.
facts.quote: The generic name refers to the River (jiang) Kai.

facts.statement: The specific name lini honors the paleontologist Lin Wenqiu.
facts.quote: The specific name honours the paleontologist Lin Wenqiu.

facts.statement: The known fossil material consists of a fragmentary skeleton that lacks the skull.
facts.quote: The specimen consists of a fragmentary skeleton lacking the skull.

facts.statement: The holotype proper includes the intercentrum of the atlas and the third through ninth cervical vertebrae.
facts.quote: The holotype proper contains the intercentrum of the atlas and the third to ninth neck vertebrae.

facts.statement: Paratypes include fragmentary skull remains, nine teeth, pectoral girdle elements, a forelimb, and a hindlimb.
facts.quote: Other elements have been designated as a paratype, including fragmentary remains of the skull, nine teeth, elements of the pectoral girdle, a forelimb, and a hindlimb.

facts.statement: A paratype consists of a thighbone belonging to a likely smaller individual.
facts.quote: Another paratype is the thighbone of a probably smaller individual.

facts.statement: Kaijiangosaurus possessed megalosaurid-type teeth with few serrations near the tip.
facts.quote: The teeth are of the megalosaurid type. Their leading edge has only few serrations, near the tip.

facts.statement: The three hand claws of Kaijiangosaurus were strongly curved.
facts.quote: The three claws of the hand are strongly curved.

facts.statement: He originally classified Kaijiangosaurus within the family Megalosauridae.
facts.quote: He originally placed Kaijiangosaurus in the Megalosauridae.

facts.statement: Modern analyses suggest Kaijiangosaurus is a basal member of Tetanurae or possibly Averostra.
facts.quote: Modern analysis suggests it is a basal member of the Tetanurae, or perhaps the Averostra.

facts.statement: Due to fragmentary remains, it is uncertain whether Kaijiangosaurus is a specific type of tetanuran theropod, though it may be a primitive carnosaur.
facts.quote: Due to the fragmentary nature of the remains, it is uncertain what type of tetanuran theropod it is, though it may be a primitive carnosaur.

facts.statement: The validity of Kaijiangosaurus is debated, with suggestions that it is a synonym of Gasosaurus or Xuanhanosaurus.
facts.quote: There have been doubts about the validity of Kaijiangosaurus. It has been suggested that it should be regarded as a synonym of Gasosaurus, which was found in the same strata as Kaijiangosaurus, the Lower Shaximiao Formation, or of Xuanhanosaurus.

facts.statement: Kaijiangosaurus lived during the Middle Jurassic, approximately 165 to 161 million years ago (Bathonian and Callovian stages), in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a mediados del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 165 a 161 millones de años en el Bathoniense y Calloviense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: Some researchers suggest Kaijiangosaurus may be an ancestor of carnosaurs based on its cervical vertebrae showing both carnosaurian and primitive traits.
facts.quote: Solo conocido por un vértebra platycoela del cuello, que presenta caracteres de carnosaurio y otros más primitivos, lo que ha llevado a pensar que es uno de los ancestros de estos.

rejected.quote: Kaijiangosaurus (meaning "Kaijiang lizard") is a genus of carnivorous tetanuran theropod dinosaur from the Middle Jurassic of China.
